blocks.passage:
In practice, a documentary collection is a simpler animal than a letter of credit, but it asks more from the two sides. The bank sends the documents, but it does not guarantee payment. That means the seller still needs to know, before shipping, that the buyer will pay when the documents arrive.

Many teams who are used to LCs find collections refreshing: less paperwork, fewer fees, faster cycles. But those same teams also learn that collections punish carelessness. A buyer who quietly decides not to pay can leave the seller with goods stuck at the destination port, with all the costs of shipping back or selling at a discount.

Collections work beautifully with trusted partners — and poorly with anyone else.

items.q: How does a documentary collection compare with a letter of credit?
options: It is simpler, but asks more from the two sides
items.why: "a documentary collection is a simpler animal than a letter of credit, but it asks more from the two sides."

items.q: What does the bank NOT do in a collection?
items.why: "The bank sends the documents, but it does not guarantee payment."

items.q: Why do teams used to LCs find collections refreshing?
options: Less paperwork, fewer fees, faster cycles
items.why: "less paperwork, fewer fees, faster cycles."

items.q: What is the risk if a buyer decides not to pay?
options: The seller is left with goods stuck at the destination port
items.why: "can leave the seller with goods stuck at the destination port."

items.q: When do collections work well?
items.why: "Collections work beautifully with trusted partners — and poorly with anyone else."

audio.text:
I'm going to show you how to fill in the collection instructions, because this is for our long-term buyer in France — someone we've dealt with for years and trust completely. That trust is exactly why a collection makes sense here.

First, decide the type. Because we trust them, we'll use documents against acceptance — D/A. That means the buyer gets the documents, and therefore the goods, in exchange for a signed promise to pay in sixty days. With a new buyer I'd never do that; I'd insist on documents against payment. But with this client, D/A is fine.

Second, name the banks clearly. Our bank is the remitting bank; theirs is the collecting bank. Get one detail wrong here and the documents go to the wrong place.

Third, write clear instructions on what to do if they don't accept: in our case, contact us immediately, do not release the documents, and hold them at the bank.

The key thing to remember: a collection is only as safe as the buyer. With this one, we're comfortable. With most, we wouldn't be.

items.q: Why does a collection make sense for this buyer?
options: It's a long-term buyer they trust completely
items.why: "our long-term buyer in France — someone we've dealt with for years and trust completely."

items.q: What type of collection does Emily choose?
items.why: "we'll use documents against acceptance — D/A."

items.q: What does D/A mean for the buyer here?
options: They get the documents in exchange for a signed promise to pay in sixty days
items.why: "the buyer gets the documents… in exchange for a signed promise to pay in sixty days."

items.q: What would Emily insist on with a new buyer?
items.why: "With a new buyer I'd never do that; I'd insist on documents against payment."

items.q: What is Emily's key point about collections?
options: A collection is only as safe as the buyer
items.why: "a collection is only as safe as the buyer."

items.q: The **remitting bank** is…
options: the seller's bank that sends the documents
items.why: Remitting bank = banco remetente (do vendedor).

items.q: A **sight draft** is paid…
items.why: Sight draft = saque à vista, pago na apresentação.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "With a time draft, the buyer signs an **___** to pay later."
items.why: Acceptance = aceite, compromisso de pagar no prazo.

items.q: "If the buyer refuses to pay, they **dishonour** the draft." To dishonour means to…
items.why: To dishonour = não honrar.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The **collecting bank** presents the documents to the…"
items.why: Collecting bank = banco cobrador, apresenta ao comprador.

items.q: "With this client, we're **comfortable**." To be comfortable with something means to…
options: be confident and at ease with it
items.why: Be comfortable with = sentir-se seguro/tranquilo.

items.q: "A buyer might **back out** of paying." To back out means to…
items.why: Back out = desistir, sair do acordo.

items.q: "Don't **release** the documents until they accept." To release documents means to…
items.why: Release = liberar, entregar.

items.q: "Collections **punish carelessness**." This means careless work…
items.why: Punish carelessness = o descuido custa caro.

items.q: "We've **dealt with** them for years." To deal with someone means to…
items.why: Deal with = negociar/lidar com.
